rv.q: Shapiro draws fine performances from the ensemble.

Are You Now or Have You Ever Been? at Arena Stage is a riveting, engrossing, and chillingly à propos docudrama that brings the dark history of McCarthyism into unsettling proximity with our own times.
This brisk, often funny docudrama about a 1940s and ’50s Congressional inquisition feels all too topical today.
Yet, despite a talented ensemble cast, the formula grows stale.
While Are You Now or Have You Ever Been? has good intentions and is a worthwhile history lesson, I’d like for more of my plays to be more like plays.

cn.t: This docudrama about HUAC hearings feels timely and riveting to some critics, though others find it more like attending a congressional hearing than compelling theater. Praise centers on its brisk pace and resonance with current events.
